title: 12 Best Speaker Management Software for B2B Event Teams | Zuddl Blog
summary: Compare 12 speaker management tools for B2B events. Covers portal branding, task automation, CRM sync, pricing, and verified gaps for each platform.
body_markdown:
‍


Your keynote speaker never uploaded their headshot. The session moderator still has last year's bio on the event page. Three sponsors are asking where to send their booth assets, and each one got a different answer from a different team member. The event is in nine days.


Speaker management software handles more than speaker profiles. It coordinates the data collection, task tracking, communication, and approval workflows that connect dozens of speakers, sponsors, and internal stakeholders across months of pre-event preparation. The complexity scales with every added track, sponsor tier, and speaker slot, and the manual coordination cost grows proportionally with each one.


This article evaluates 12 speaker management tools across portal branding and customization, task and asset collection automation, and lead capture with CRM sync, among other operational dimensions. Each entry covers verified capabilities, documented gaps, pricing, and the specific team situation each tool fits best.

## The 12 best speaker management software for B2B event teams


### Zuddl


Zuddl is the AI-native unified events platform with speaker and exhibitor portals designed for full brand control across every attendee-facing touchpoint. It is made for B2B event teams running conferences, field events, and webinars for anywhere between 100 to 25,000+ attendees who need speaker coordination, sponsor management, and lead capture operating inside a single system with one shared data layer.


**What it does well**


- [Speaker and exhibitor portals can be white-labeled with logos, fonts, themes, and custom URLs](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-speaker-and-exhibitor-portal) so the portal experience matches the registration site, mobile app, and badge design rather than looking like a third-party tool.


- Task auto-assignment by sponsor tier means creating a task and linking it to a specific tier automatically assigns it to every matching sponsor, including new sponsors added to that tier later, removing manual tracking from the coordinator's workload.


- Dry run mode lets speakers and organizers rehearse before going live, simulating a full session with audio, video, and content-sharing checks so technical failures surface in rehearsal instead of during a live keynote.


- [Bi-directional CRM sync with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Eloqua](https://www.zuddl.com/event-integrations) pushes registrations, engagement data, and attendee activity into CRM in real time, so sponsor follow-up starts while the session is still running rather than days after the event closes.


- Speakers and sponsors can access[self-serve session analytics and lead analytics](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-analytics) directly inside the portal, eliminating the post-event cycle of manually pulling and distributing performance reports to every stakeholder.


**Where it has gaps**


- Zuddl does not include a call-for-papers or abstract submission workflow


**Pricing:** Entry-level starts at $10,000/year (webinars) or $12,000/year (conferences), priced on annual attendee volume with no per-event or per-registration fees.[See pricing](https://www.zuddl.com/pricing)


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams replacing separate tools for speaker coordination, sponsor portals, and lead capture who want one branded platform where speakers self-serve tasks, sponsors access real-time leads, and CRM data flows without manual export.


### Bizzabo


Bizzabo provides a dedicated speaker portal with centralized task management and automated reminders, positioned for teams managing hundreds of speakers across enterprise conferences. It fits mid-to-large B2B event teams running multi-track programs who need speaker coordination alongside registration and agenda management.


**What it does well**


- A branded, self-service speaker portal supports any number of speakers, letting event teams scale coordination for large conferences without proportionally scaling admin effort.


- Centralized task management with automated reminders handles bio collection, headshot uploads, and session material delivery, with a custom VIP portal for managing hundreds of speakers.


- Blog-documented workflows describe automated tasks, approvals, and reminders as part of speaker onboarding and preparation, covering the pre-event communication cycle.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-page evidence found for exhibitor or sponsor lead capture tools or CRM sync, which limits visibility into whether sponsor engagement data can flow into marketing automation systems.


- No documented session lineup or schedule coordination capability was found on the pages reviewed, making it unclear how session changes propagate across web and mobile surfaces.


- Multiple Capterra reviewers note limited flexibility in customizing certain portal and branding elements without vendor assistance.


- Pricing is fully custom with no published figures, which several G2 and Capterra reviewers flag as a barrier to budgeting, particularly for recurring events.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Enterprise B2B event teams managing large speaker rosters who need a dedicated VIP speaker portal with automated task reminders and centralized content collection, and who have budget flexibility for custom-quoted pricing.


### Cvent


Cvent offers a Speaker Resource Center that centralizes speaker task management with branded reminders and a reusable speaker profile library. It serves large enterprise event operations running recurring conferences where speaker data needs to carry over across events.


**What it does well**


- The Speaker Resource Center automates speaker management tasks, collects all speaker content in one central location, and generates reports on task completion with branded reminders sent when deadlines are lagging.


- Tasks can be created with flexibility to assign them to all speakers or individual ones, covering both bulk and targeted coordination needs.


- An account-level speaker profile library stores speaker data for reuse across events, reducing repeated data collection for organizations with returning speaker rosters.


- Resource management helps prevent double-booking of speakers across sessions, addressing a common scheduling failure in multi-track conference programs.


**Where it has gaps**


- Multiple G2 reviewers describe the platform as unintuitive for new admins, with a steep learning curve that affects teams managing speakers and exhibitors for the first time.


- Capterra reviewers note that support for speaker and exhibitor self-service tasks (uploading assets, tracking status) can feel manual and email-driven rather than fully automated.


- No backstage, green room, or AV tech-check capability was found on the speaker management pages reviewed.


- Add-on modules such as speaker management extras increase total spend beyond the base platform, a concern flagged repeatedly by Capterra reviewers.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Large enterprise event operations running recurring annual conferences with returning speaker rosters, where a reusable profile library and centralized task tracking matter more than portal branding flexibility or live production tools.


### Whova


Whova combines speaker management with an abstract submission system and a widely adopted attendee-facing mobile app. It fits B2B conference organizers who need speaker submissions to flow directly into a published agenda and event app without manual re-entry.


**What it does well**


- Speaker form data auto-populates bios, session descriptions, handouts, and profile photos directly into the event app and speaker webpage, removing the manual step of re-entering speaker content across surfaces.


- Accepted call-for-speakers submissions import directly into the event schedule with distinguishable tracks and tags, supporting multi-track conferences with hundreds of sessions.


- Automated notifications for rejections, acceptances, and revision requests keep speakers informed about submission status without manual email follow-up.


**Where it has gaps**


- No evidence of white-label control or custom branding of the speaker portal was found. Several reviewers note limited customization of design and branding elements relative to competitors.


- No exhibitor or sponsor lead capture or CRM sync capability was documented on the speaker management pages reviewed.


- Pricing is not transparent and requires sales contact, a recurring complaint across both G2 and Capterra reviews.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B conference teams running multi-track programs with a call for speakers or abstract submission process who need accepted submissions to auto-populate into a mobile event app and agenda without manual data transfer.


### InEvent


InEvent provides a speaker management module with automated task assignment and an integrated agenda builder that applies schedule changes instantly. It serves teams running hybrid or virtual conferences who need speaker coordination tied directly to session scheduling.


**What it does well**


- Automated task assignment and tracking with self-service profile and session management lets speakers handle their own data updates without waiting for organizer intervention.


- The integrated agenda builder allows organizers to move, reschedule, or swap speakers with instant updates, so attendees always see the current schedule rather than a stale version.


- Bulk communication and reminders with automated, personalized email or app notifications reduce the volume of one-off messages coordinators send manually.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-page evidence found for portal branding or white-label customization of the speaker-facing experience.


- No backstage, green room, or AV tech-check capability was documented on the pages reviewed.


- No exhibitor lead capture or CRM sync capability was found on the speaker management pages, though exhibitor-specific product pages were not in scope for this review.


- Some G2 reviewers note a learning curve for the admin backend given the breadth of features.


**Pricing:** Starting from $9,990/year.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running hybrid conferences who need speaker task automation tied directly to a schedule builder that updates instantly when sessions shift, and who prioritize agenda coordination over sponsor-facing portal features.


### Sessionboard


Sessionboard is a purpose-built speaker and content management CRM with call for papers, multi-round peer review, and a speaker history database that tracks contributions across years and formats. It fits conference teams that manage recurring speaker relationships and need submission workflows separate from their event management platform.


**What it does well**


- A speaker CRM tracks speaker history, content, and contributions across multiple years and formats, giving program committees a persistent database rather than starting from scratch each event cycle.


- Personalized speaker portals let speakers update bios, upload files, complete tasks, and see deadlines in one place, with SSO authentication through existing identity providers.


- Call for papers includes submission tracking, reviewer assignment, scoring across multiple review rounds, and AI-assisted evaluation to score and rank submissions against defined criteria.


- Visual scheduling with conflict detection and room placement supports agenda assembly after submissions are accepted.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-page evidence found for white-label portal branding or visual customization of the speaker-facing portal beyond functional personalization.


- No backstage, green room, or live production tools documented. Sessionboard focuses on pre-event content and speaker management rather than day-of delivery.


- No G2 profile exists and Capterra shows zero reviews, meaning no independent third-party validation of any capability claim is available.


**Pricing:** $249/month (Professional plan).


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Conference program teams managing recurring speaker relationships across annual events who need a dedicated speaker CRM with multi-year tracking, structured peer review, and integration with platforms like Cvent or Bizzabo rather than a replacement for them.


### Cadmium


Cadmium (Eventscribe) is an abstract and speaker management platform built for associations and organizations running CE/CME-accredited events with structured peer review workflows. It fits teams whose speaker management starts with abstract submission and reviewer coordination rather than direct speaker invitations.


**What it does well**


- A task-based portal gives speakers visibility into what they need to complete and when it is due, structuring the collection process around deadlines rather than ad-hoc email requests.


- Abstract submission and review workflows support submitters and reviewers in one tool, covering the full path from submission to acceptance for association-style conference programs.


- Integrates with top AMS and AV providers, connecting speaker and content data to the systems associations already use for membership and event delivery.


**Where it has gaps**


- No explicit white-label or visual branding control of the speaker portal was documented. Capterra reviewers note that customization of speaker and exhibitor-facing pages requires vendor assistance rather than being fully self-serve.


- Several G2 reviewers describe the interface as dated compared to newer platforms, with a steep learning curve for first-time admins.


- No evidence of exhibitor lead capture tools or CRM sync (Salesforce, HubSpot) was found on the pages reviewed. Integration claims reference AMS and AV providers only.


- Both G2 (21 reviews) and Capterra (26 reviews) have small review volumes, limiting confidence in any single review theme.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Association and medical conference teams running CE/CME-accredited programs where abstract peer review, disclosure management, and AMS integration are central to the speaker management workflow, and where branding flexibility is less critical than submission process rigor.


### Lineup Ninja


Lineup Ninja is a speaker scheduling and conference content management platform with custom workflow builders and clash detection for multi-track agendas. It fits conference content teams managing large programs where speaker scheduling conflicts and content collection are the primary operational risks.


**What it does well**


- Custom workflows let teams build their own content collection process and automate speaker communication and tracking tasks, adapting to different conference formats rather than following a fixed template.


- A content portal gives speakers a single place for tasks and communication, with the ability to gather slides in one location and share them with reviewers and AV technicians.


- A smart agenda builder tracks each session's scheduling needs and alerts organizers to conflicts, with speaker availability and clash detection built in as standard functionality.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-page evidence found for portal branding, white-labeling, or visual customization of the speaker-facing content portal.


- No backstage, green room, or live production tools documented. Lineup Ninja's scope covers pre-event content and agenda management, not live session delivery.


- No exhibitor lead capture or CRM sync capability was found. The platform focuses on speaker and content coordination, not sponsor engagement.


- G2 has only 1 review and Capterra has 7, making independent review-based validation of any capability claim unreliable.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 5.0/5 on G2 · 5.0/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Conference content managers running large multi-track programs who need configurable speaker submission workflows, automated clash detection, and centralized slide collection, and who already use a separate platform for registration, sponsor management, and live production.


### Sched


Sched is an event scheduling platform where speakers self-manage profiles, upload presentations, and respond to session assignments through a structured call for papers workflow. It fits mid-size conference organizers who need scheduling, speaker coordination, and attendee-facing agendas at a lower price point than enterprise platforms.


**What it does well**


- Speakers can upload presentation files directly to session pages and customize their own profiles with photos, bios, and social links, reducing the data collection load on organizers.


- A call for papers feature includes customizable submission forms, multi-speaker submission tracking, and committee review, handling the intake process for conferences accepting external session proposals.


- Scheduling automation handles room assignment and conflict checking, with an interactive schedule that lets attendees build personal agendas from available sessions.


**Where it has gaps**


- Branding customization is gated behind higher-tier plans (Boost at $1,499/year and above), with no evidence of full white-label portal restyling at any tier.


- No exhibitor lead capture or CRM sync capability was found on the vendor's public-facing pages.


- No backstage, green room, or virtual production tools documented. Sched is oriented toward in-person and hybrid conference logistics rather than virtual session delivery.


- G2 reviewers note the admin interface feels dated, and some Capterra reviewers mention that advanced features require higher-cost plans.


**Pricing:** $599/year (Launch Plan). Boost plan at $1,499/year, Ultra at $3,899/year. 30-day free trial available.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Mid-size B2B conference teams running multi-day, multi-track events who need an affordable scheduling platform with built-in call for papers and speaker self-service, and who do not require sponsor lead capture or live virtual production tools.


### Sessionize


Sessionize is a call for papers and speaker management tool focused on submission collection, speaker coordination, and schedule building. It serves conference organizers whose primary speaker management need is processing external session proposals and building an agenda from accepted submissions.


**What it does well**


- Call for papers management with the ability to edit all session and speaker information in one place, covering the full cycle from submission intake to schedule publication.


- Drag-and-drop scheduling with the option to embed the schedule on a website as JSON or XML, plus a mobile app with schedule generation, gives organizers multiple publishing options for the final agenda.


- Speakers can edit or add their own information, and the platform builds speaker profiles with speaking history, reducing organizer data-entry work across recurring events.


**Where it has gaps**


- No portal branding, white-label, or visual customization capability documented. Sessionize does not appear to offer restyling of the speaker-facing experience.


- No exhibitor, sponsor, or lead capture functionality exists. The feature set addresses speakers and sessions only.


- No backstage, green room, or live production tools. Sessionize is a pre-event CFP and scheduling tool, not a live delivery platform.


- No G2 listing exists and Capterra shows zero reviews, providing no independent validation of any capability claim.


**Pricing:** $499 per event occurrence. Free trial available.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Conference organizers running community or industry events who need a focused call for papers tool with drag-and-drop scheduling and embeddable agendas, and who handle sponsor management, branding, and live production through other systems.


### CATALYST Abstract & Speaker Management Software


CATALYST, a product of Omnipress, is an abstract and speaker management tool for academic, scientific, and medical conferences with structured peer review requirements. It fits organizations running large annual meetings where abstract submission quality, multi-round review scoring, and conflict-free scheduling are the defining operational challenges.


**What it does well**


- Drag-and-drop scheduling assigns sessions and builds the conference agenda, with room and speaker conflict detection built in for managing complex multi-track programs.


- Configurable workflow supports blind reviews, custom scoring, and multi-round submissions, giving program committees control over the peer review process without external tools.


- Role-based dashboards for event managers, submitters, and reviewers provide visibility into submission status at each level of the workflow.


**Where it has gaps**


- No explicit white-label or portal branding capability documented. Form configurability is confirmed, but visual branding of the speaker-facing experience is not addressed.


- No automated task assignment, tier-based reminders, or asset collection workflows for speakers or exhibitors were found on the pages reviewed.


- No exhibitor lead capture or CRM integration capability documented. CATALYST is scoped to abstract and speaker submission management, not sponsor engagement.


- No G2 or Capterra reviews are available, providing no independent validation of any capability claim.


**Pricing:** $7 to $15 per submission (tiered by volume), plus a $3,500 flat site setup and project management support fee.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Academic, scientific, or medical conference teams running structured abstract peer review with multi-round scoring and conflict-free scheduling requirements, where submission rigor matters more than sponsor coordination or branded portal experiences.


### X-CD


X-CD is a conference management platform with deep speaker data collection capabilities, including abstract management, disclosure tracking, and wireless presentation delivery. It fits scientific and medical conference teams managing large volumes of speaker files, agreements, and compliance documents.


**What it does well**


- Collects abstracts, papers, PowerPoint presentations, ePosters, videos, handouts, and unlimited additional file types from event speakers, covering the full range of content a scientific conference requires.


- Tracks speaker agreements and communicates with speakers who are missing forms or disclosures, addressing compliance requirements common in medical and scientific events.


- Pushes PowerPoint presentations wirelessly directly to correct session rooms, reducing the AV coordination burden during multi-room conference days.


**Where it has gaps**


- No evidence found for automated speaker communication workflows such as trigger-based status notifications, calendar automation, or approval routing.


- No self-serve analytics for speakers or sponsors was documented on the pages reviewed.


- No exhibitor lead capture or CRM sync capability was found. X-CD's feature set focuses on speaker content collection and conference scheduling.


- No G2 profile exists and Capterra rating data is not available, providing no independent review-based validation.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Scientific and medical conference organizers managing large speaker pools where disclosure tracking, unlimited file collection, and wireless presentation delivery to session rooms are operational priorities, and where sponsor-facing workflows are handled separately.


## What to look for in speaker management software for B2B event teams


1. **Speaker/exhibitor portal branding and customization:** Evaluate whether the speaker portal can carry your event brand (logos, colors, URLs) without developer help. A generic, vendor-branded portal creates visual inconsistency between registration, app, and speaker experience.


1. **Speaker/sponsor task and asset collection automation.** Check whether tasks (bios, headshots, signed agreements, presentations) can be auto-assigned by role or tier and tracked with automated reminders. Without this, coordinators revert to spreadsheets and manual email chasing.


1. **Automated speaker communication and status flows.** Look for[trigger-based notifications covering confirmations, reminders, and schedule changes](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/event-communications) . Manual email blasts for speaker updates cause no-shows and confusion when session times shift.


1. **Session lineup and schedule coordination.** Confirm that speaker or session changes update across the event website, mobile app, and portal simultaneously. Separate manual edits across surfaces lead to outdated agendas reaching attendees and speakers.


1. **Live event speaker readiness and backstage support.** Check for virtual green rooms,[dry run capabilities, and one-click join links for external speakers](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/virtual-and-hybrid-events/video-production-and-streaming) . Without backstage tools, a speaker's audio failure becomes visible to the audience before the organizer can intervene.


1. **Self-serve analytics for speakers and sponsors.** Determine whether speakers and sponsors can independently view their own[session attendance and engagement data](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/lead-capture) . If they cannot, the event team becomes a bottleneck for distributing post-event reports.


1. **Exhibitor/sponsor lead capture and CRM sync.** Verify whether[sponsor lead data syncs bi-directionally into CRM systems](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/universal-lead-capture) like Salesforce or HubSpot. Disconnected lead data forces manual export and delays follow-up while sales interest decays.


1. **Role-based access and partner/sponsor self-sufficiency.** Evaluate whether sponsors and partners can manage their own portal scope (uploading assets, adding team members, viewing their data) without the organizer creating individual accounts. For events with dozens of sponsors, manual access provisioning becomes a bottleneck.


## Questions people ask about speaker management software


**What is the difference between speaker management software and event management software?**


Event management software covers registration, ticketing, venue logistics, and attendee engagement across the full event lifecycle. Speaker management software focuses specifically on coordinating speakers: collecting bios and presentations, assigning tasks, managing session scheduling, and handling communication workflows. Some platforms like Zuddl and Cvent include speaker management as a module within a broader event platform, while tools like Sessionboard and Sessionize operate as dedicated speaker coordination systems.


**What are the key features of speaker management software?**


The most operationally significant features are task and asset collection automation (bios, headshots, signed agreements),[branded speaker portals for self-service](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/branding-events) , automated communication flows for reminders and status updates, session scheduling with conflict detection, and self-serve analytics so speakers can view their own session performance. For B2B events with sponsors, lead capture tools and CRM sync add a layer that connects speaker sessions to measurable pipeline outcomes.


**Can I use speaker management software alongside event management platforms like Cvent or Bizzabo?**


Yes. Dedicated speaker management tools like Sessionboard and Lineup Ninja are designed to integrate with platforms like Cvent and Bizzabo, handling speaker content collection and scheduling while the event platform manages registration and attendee experience. Sessionboard lists 15 or more integrations including Cvent and Bizzabo. Zuddl takes a different approach by including[speaker and exhibitor management natively](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/session-management) , eliminating the need for a separate integration layer.


**What are the benefits of implementing speaker management software?**


The primary benefit is removing manual coordination from the speaker workflow. Instead of emailing individual speakers about missing headshots, tracking task completion in spreadsheets, or manually updating session changes across multiple pages, speaker management software automates assignment, reminders, and schedule propagation. For B2B event teams, this reduces coordinator hours, minimizes the risk of outdated content reaching attendees, and gives sponsors and speakers direct visibility into their own data.
